title: Quant profile ingestion index and SLO smokechecks
creator: Aisha K. Patel
description: Build a small, testable pipeline and index for newly generated quantization performance profiles (INT8, FP8, GPTQ, AWQ) and attach a lightweight SLO smokecheck that runs on onboarding profiles. Goal: detect major perf regressions (latency >+30%, throughput <-20%, memory spike) before profiles are published to the model catalog. This ticket covers ingestion schema, index format, quick validation hooks, and a first-pass alerting dashboard for regressions.
motivation: We regularly surface quant profiles from different calibration runs. Without a canonical index + fast smoke validation, bad profiles (e.g., broken kernel selection or catastrophic latency regressions) slip into catalog pins and cause customer incidents. A fast gating step reduces blast radius and developer toil.
acceptance_criteria: New quant profile artifacts (INT8/FP8/GPTQ/AWQ) are written to the 'quant-profile-index' with metadata: model_id, model_hash, profile_type, seq_len_distribution, perf_summary, commit_ref, and created_at
A smokecheck job executes within 90s of index write and emits a pass/fail plus perf deltas vs baseline for latency, p95, tokens/sec, and peak GPU memory
Failing smokechecks create an alert in the onboarding dashboard and write a short failure_reason into the index record
Profiles that pass smokechecks automatically get a 'candidate' tag but do not propagate to the public pin registry until further verification
End-to-end tests (unit + integration) cover INT8 and GPTQ sample artifacts and run in CI with synthetic kernels mocked
Documentation page (Confluence) describes index schema, validation thresholds, and how to override during manual audits
implementation_notes: Index will be a compact JSONL store backed by existing metadata-db migration to avoid a new service
Smokecheck runs lightweight bench harness using 2 fixed prompts (short/long) and samples of kv-cache sizes to exercise kernel paths
Baseline metrics pulled from model's current pinned profile; if none exist, use model family baseline table
Use existing telemetry pipeline (telemetry-v2) to emit onboarding metrics with a new namespace 'quant.ingest'
We will tag each profile with a 'profiling_commit' that references the PR that produced it for auditability
testing_plan: Unit: schema validation, index write/read, failure_reason parsing
Integration: ingest synthetic INT8 and GPTQ artifacts in CI; run smokecheck; assert candidate tag and failure_reason behavior
Staging: run against small set of real models (gpt-small, falcon-7b) with real kernels; validate dashboard alerts
Performance: ensure smokecheck completes < 90s for 95% of cases on staging infra
rollout_plan: Feature branch + PR with unit tests (eng review)
Merge to canary branch and run integration pipeline (2 engineers)
Deploy index migration and enable smokecheck for 10% of new artifacts for 48h
Expand to 100% after 48h if failure rate < 2% and no customer impact reported
Manual audit and retro after first week; refine thresholds or add additional prompts as needed
updates: 2025-02-18: Ticket created. Initial scoping done with Research (J. Kim) and Runtime (L. Ortega). Decided to reuse metadata-db to avoid new service overhead.
2025-02-24: Schema proposal v1 posted to Confluence. Telemetry schema agreed with infra-team (namespaced under quant.ingest).
2025-02-27: Design review: agreed to run two synthetic prompts to capture short/long path behavior. Trade-off: fewer prompts speed up smokecheck but reduce statistical coverage.
2025-03-01: PR opened for index writer and schema validation (GH #4821). CI unit tests passing; integration tests failing on mocked GPU env (investigating kernel path mismatch).
2025-03-04: Decided to add a fallback baseline selection: if model family baseline missing, use 'family-proxy' derived from nearest family median to avoid false positives for brand-new models.
2025-03-05: QA scheduled for 2025-03-07 to run staging ingestion on falcon-7b sample artifacts. Liam to follow up on infra quota for quick bench jobs.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Smokecheck may produce false positives for long-tail models -> Mitigation: add family-proxy baseline and a manual 'override' workflow
Risk: Index write failures could block ingestion pipeline -> Mitigation: implement retry + dead-letter queue and surface failures to SRE channel
Risk: Telemetry cardinality growth -> Mitigation: only emit aggregate deltas and sample raw traces for 1% of ingests
review_feedback: PM (Erin Jansen): favor conservative fail thresholds for first two weeks and add an explicit 'manual audit' tag on failing profiles
Research (Jon Kim): requested we include sample outputs (tokens) in the index for future quality evaluations; agreed to include hashes only for now
Security (R. Singh): no immediate concerns but requested we avoid storing raw payloads in index (we will only store metrics and artifact refs)
